title: A heavier spring oscillator
hook: Change attached mass and predict oscillation period.
misconception: oscillation period doubles when attached mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply T = 2π√(m/k) to compare oscillation period when attached mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal horizontal spring with fixed stiffness, T = 2π√(m/k). When attached mass doubles, oscillation period becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model T = 2π√(m/k); scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal horizontal spring with fixed stiffness, with a nonzero initial result. If attached mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on oscillation period?
recall.why: Apply T = 2π√(m/k) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
